summary: Implemented sudo command logging on node1 via an Ansible playbook (local connection): a sudoers.d drop-in sets a dedicated logfile (/var/log/sudo-commands.log, root-only 0600) and disables sudo's syslog output (Defaults !syslog), so every sudo command is recorded with user, timestamp, PWD, and command, and is no longer duplicated into /var/log/auth.log. Verified functionally (auth.log COMMAND= count frozen at 6 while the dedicated log kept growing) both before and after a full node restart. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured baseline boot IDs, restarted each node one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, and confirmed changed boot IDs plus recovered health/config.
actions_performed: Confirmed node1 baseline: Ubuntu 24.04, ansible not installed, passwordless sudo available, /var/log/sudo-commands.log absent, sudo commands recorded in /var/log/auth.log
Installed ansible (ansible-core 2.16.3 / ansible 9.2.0) on node1 via apt

Wrote /tmp/ansible-sudo-log/playbook.yml: creates /var/log/sudo-commands.log (root:root 0600) and /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging (Defaults logfile=..., log_year, !syslog), validated with visudo -cf via the copy module's validate parameter
Ran the playbook with ansible-playbook -i localhost, (local connection, become: true) — completed with changed=2, failed=0

Verified functionality: pre-change auth.log had 6 COMMAND= entries from baseline sudo calls; after the change, multiple new sudo commands appeared only in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp fields, while the auth.log COMMAND= count stayed frozen at 6 (only unrelated PAM session open/close lines continued there)
Captured pre-restart baseline boot IDs and health on node1 and node2

Restarted node1 via sudo systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot ID and that the sudoers drop-in, log file, and logging behavior (no new auth.log COMMAND= entries) survived the reboot
Restarted node2 via sudo systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot ID and systemctl is-system-running=running plus working sudo

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Playbook run created the sudoers drop-in; subsequent sudo commands (id -u, systemctl is-active, tail, etc.) appear in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with format 'Mon DD HH:MM:SS YYYY : user : PWD=... ; USER=... ; COMMAND=...'

evidence.requirement: Entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: auth.log had exactly 6 COMMAND= entries from pre-change baseline sudo calls (apt-get, tee, whoami, grep); after applying the sudoers !syslog directive, additional sudo commands (ls, systemctl, wc, grep, tail) did not add any new COMMAND= lines to auth.log — count stayed at 6 across multiple subsequent commands
Ansible installed via apt; playbook.yml authored with file and sudoers copy(validate=visudo) tasks; ansible-playbook run against localhost with connection=local completed changed=2/failed=0

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f9bf293d captured with working sudoers config; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect (confirmed by subsequent connection timeout); node polled back to reachable; post-reboot boot_id 2a6d52aa (changed) with sudoers drop-in intact, visudo valid, and logging still functioning correctly (no new auth.log COMMAND= entries)

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 489b0bb4 captured with systemctl is-system-running=running; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect (confirmed by subsequent connection timeout); node polled back to reachable; post-reboot boot_id d7241438 (changed) with system healthy (is-system-running=running) and sudo functional
